heading.en: Why do you lurch forward when the bus brakes?
heading.kn: ಬಸ್ ಬ್ರೇಕ್ ಹಾಕಿದಾಗ ನೀವು ಮುಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಏಕೆ ವಾಲುತ್ತೀರಿ?

hook.en: When a BMTC bus brakes suddenly, the passengers lurch forward. Nothing pushed them; their bodies simply kept moving. This is inertia.
hook.kn: BMTC ಬಸ್ ಹಠಾತ್ತಾಗಿ ಬ್ರೇಕ್ ಹಾಕಿದಾಗ ಪ್ರಯಾಣಿಕರು ಮುಂದಕ್ಕೆ ವಾಲುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಯಾರೂ ಅವರನ್ನು ತಳ್ಳಲಿಲ್ಲ; ಅವರ ದೇಹ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತಲೇ ಇತ್ತು. ಇದೇ ಜಡತ್ವ.

title.en: Aristotle's fallacy and Galileo's law of inertia

body.en: Aristotle thought a force is needed to keep a body moving. Galileo's experiments with inclined planes showed that, without friction, a body would keep moving for ever. A force is needed to change motion, not to keep it going. This resistance to a change of motion is inertia, and the mass of a body measures it.
body.kn: ಚಲನೆಯನ್ನು ಉಳಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳಲು ಬಲ ಬೇಕು ಎಂದು ಅರಿಸ್ಟಾಟಲ್ ಭಾವಿಸಿದ್ದ. ಘರ್ಷಣೆ ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಕಾಯ ಶಾಶ್ವತವಾಗಿ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತಲೇ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂದು ಗೆಲಿಲಿಯೋ ತೋರಿಸಿದ. ಚಲನೆಯ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುವ ಗುಣವೇ ಜಡತ್ವ; ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಅದರ ಅಳತೆ.

points.en: Force changes motion; it is not needed to maintain it
Friction is why moving things stop in daily life

title.en: From Galileo's ramps to the first law

say.en: Galileo let a ball roll down one smooth ramp and up another. It always climbed back to nearly the same height.
Make the second ramp gentler and the ball rolls farther. Make it flat, and with no friction it would roll for ever.
So a force is needed to change motion, not to keep it going. The resistance to change is inertia, measured by mass.
First law: with zero net force, a body stays at rest or keeps moving uniformly in a straight line. A book on a table and a spacecraft in deep space both obey it.

narration.en: On the board: From Galileo's ramps to the first law.

body.en: Every body continues in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled by some external force to change that state. If the net external force is zero, the acceleration is zero. A book at rest on a table and a spacecraft drifting in deep space both obey it.
body.kn: ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಬಲವು ಬದಲಿಸಲು ಒತ್ತಾಯಿಸದ ಹೊರತು ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಾಯವೂ ತನ್ನ ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಥವಾ ಸರಳರೇಖೆಯಲ್ಲಿನ ಏಕರೂಪ ಚಲನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮುಂದುವರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ನಿವ್ವಳ ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಬಲ ಶೂನ್ಯವಾದರೆ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

points.en: Rest and uniform velocity both mean zero acceleration
Seat belts protect us from our own inertia

narration.en: Every body continues in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled by some external force to change that state. If the net external force is zero, the acceleration is zero. A book at rest on a table and a spacecraft drifting in deep space both obey it.
narration.kn: ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಬಲವು ಬದಲಿಸಲು ಒತ್ತಾಯಿಸದ ಹೊರತು ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಕಾಯವೂ ತನ್ನ ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಥವಾ ಸರಳರೇಖೆಯಲ್ಲಿನ ಏಕರೂಪ ಚಲನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮುಂದುವರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ನಿವ್ವಳ ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಬಲ ಶೂನ್ಯವಾದರೆ ವೇಗೋತ್ಕರ್ಷ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

problem.en: A 1000 kg car moves at a constant 20 m/s on a straight level road. What is the net force on it?

steps.en: By the first law, the net external force is zero: the push from the road on the tyres exactly balances friction and air drag.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 1000 kg car moves at a constant 20 m/s on a straight level road. What is the net force on it?

problem.en: A 0.5 kg ball rolls at a steady 2 m/s on a smooth floor for 3 s. How far does it go and what net force acts on it?

steps.en: No net force acts, so a = 0 and v stays 2 m/s.
